subject: shower curtain
title: What If You Never Cleaned Your Shower Curtain?

scenes.text: What if you never cleaned your shower curtain? That pink film isn't just soap.
Scientists at the University of Colorado scraped the scum off four vinyl curtains and read the DNA.
Each curtain held a complex community. Over a tenth of the microbes found may be new kinds of bacteria.
The leaders, Sphingomonas and Methylobacterium, include germs that can sicken people with weak immune systems.
Their verdict: clean it often or throw it away.
And that curtain attacking your legs? A computer model blamed a spinning vortex from the spray. It won an Ig Nobel prize.

description:
What if you never cleaned your shower curtain? A 2004 University of Colorado study of soap scum on vinyl shower curtains found highly complex microbial communities dominated by Sphingomonas and Methylobacterium, groups that include opportunistic pathogens.
The authors recommended frequent cleaning or disposal. The curtain blowing inward was modelled as a spray-driven vortex, work that won a 2001 Ig Nobel Prize.
